tagline: Every story you love is made of sentences. Come see how they are built, tuned and set loose.

epigraph.text: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times…
epigraph.cite: Charles Dickens, A Tale of Two Cities (1859)

art.note: The council decided to keep the Baroque structural grid and iron-gall settle while allowing visible capillary feathering as the only imperfection.

writers.note: We kept the grid but let the ink bleed where the reader breathes; the workshop is a place of controlled imperfection.

nuggets.hook: A sentence with no subject is like a house with no door.
nuggets.body: Sometimes the who is hidden, but the action still happens. Try writing a sentence where the person is the secret.

nuggets.hook: Can you hear the grumpy cat in this paragraph?
nuggets.body: Voice is the personality behind the words. Swap one word and watch the character change from shy to sassy.

nuggets.hook: Don’t tell me the moon is bright. Show me the silver dust.
nuggets.body: Telling is a summary; showing is a photograph. Your job is to let the reader see the dust before they read the word bright.

nuggets.hook: Short sentences hit hard. Long sentences flow like a river.
nuggets.body: Rhythm is the heartbeat of prose. Read this line aloud and feel where your breath wants to pause.
